messages:
oncall-bot: :rotating_light: paging: KV cache growth alert (prod-us-east-1) - sustained memory increase + batching latency spike > 95th for 10m

alex.k: i'm on it. grabbing metrics and logs. who owns continuous-batcher config?

rachel.m: infra owns the flag but runtime made a recent change to auto-batch heuristics on 1802342000. could be related.

samir: seeing a ~6x increase in active KV entries for customer:enterprise-acme after rolling larger batch windows. heap growth correlates with request rate for that tenant.

alex.k: can you paste the query you used?

samir: `sum(rate(kv_cache_items{region="us-east-1"}[1m])) by (customer)` then looked at 95pct latencies: `histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(request_duration_seconds_bucket[5m])) by (le, customer))`

alex.k: confirmed. enterprise-acme steady traffic + new batch window caused cache prefix blowup. ops note: this tenant has large prompt prefixes (chat history).

jules.sre: impact assessment: increased token-cost and latency for a handful of routes (generate/chat) for that tenant only. No full cluster OOMs yet but risk of eviction storms.

rachel.m: mitigation options: 1) immediate per-customer override to reduce batch_window_ms for enterprise-acme, 2) global batch window rollback (broad), 3) add aggressive cache ttl for large-prefix entries (slower to deploy). preference is option 1 to limit blast radius.

alex.k: agree. plan: flip per-customer override via feature-flag store and push canary to a single region host. I'll coordinate with deploy-bot.

samir: commands to apply (for records):
```
# set feature flag for cust
curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN" \
  -d '{"customer":"enterprise-acme","batch_window_ms":25}' \
  https://flags.internal.redwood/api/v1/overrides

# verify
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN" https://flags.internal.redwood/api/v1/overrides?customer=enterprise-acme
```

alex.k: applying override to region us-east-1 (canary host group: batch-group-a). will watch telemetry for 2m, then expand if stable.

deploy-bot: deploy request accepted. canary started on host batch-a-3. link: https://deploys.internal/1802345678

rachel.m: telemetry: batch_size p50 down from 18->3 for the customer on the canary host; KV insertion rate halved. latency 95pct improving.

alex.k: expanding to remaining hosts in us-east-1.

samir: also adding a transient throttle in the routing layer for the affected routes for enterprise-acme (soft-fail to queued path) to reduce immediate pressure. command: `kubectl patch svc batch-router -p '{"spec":{"env":[{"name":"PER_CUST_THROTTLE","value":"enterprise-acme:0.6"}]}}'`

jules.sre: FYI re customer impact comms: product should be notified if we engage per-customer throttles; I'll ping solutions-eng to prep a note.

alex.k: monitoring shows no OOMs, mem usage declining. keeping canary at 5m to be safe.

rachel.m: once us-east stable, we should roll to other regions with automated rollout policy: 20%->50%->100% with 3m observation windows. I'll upload the rollout plan to the incident doc.

samir: after 12m, KV growth for enterprise-acme plateaued and started decaying. cost telemetry shows token spend normalized.

alex.k: thanks. closing immediate mitigation after final validation. next actions:
- create postmortem with root cause (auto-batcher heuristics + large-prefix tenant)
- recommend conservative defaults and per-customer sampling guard rails
- add alert for per-customer KV growth (not only cluster-level)
- customer outreach: solutions-eng to draft a note

jules.sre: tagging for follow-up: #postmortem, #customer-comms, #runbook-update

rachel.m: short-term config diff that caused this: `auto_batch: {min_window_ms: 20, max_window_ms: 200, growth_factor: 1.8}`. growth_factor tweak pushed two days ago. recommend clamp growth_factor to <=1.2 until we add prefix-size heuristic.

alex.k: any objections to marking incident as mitigated and moving to monitoring?

samir: none. :thumbsup:

oncall-bot: incident mitigated by alex.k. Severity: Sev2 -> Monitoring. incident-channel: #incidents-1802345678

alex.k: moving to write the timeline & RCA. will assign owners for each follow-up. thanks all for quick handling. :rocket:
